payload.title: The rating classifier decides three stars or better
payload.description:
**Planning story.** Decision (Ryan, 2026-11-13): "The main classifier going on will be to decide if an item is three-stars (average) or better." The default rating is three stars. The relevance Cyclotron's question for Stories and References becomes "is this item at least three stars?" (at-least-three versus below-three), not a generic accept/reject.

Related: PPY-0e8d66 (three-star floor on public pages), PPY-3247f1 (Reference stars), PPY-d89268 and PPY-3ba823 (Story stars CLI), the new story 'A machine never assigns five stars' (this one depends on it), PPY-0a285b (shared cyclotron with a classifier per Section), PPY-b2b73e (reporting agents steer classifiers), docs/cyclotron-priming.md, docs/reference-curation-pipeline.md.

**Rules already in force (unchanged).** An item with no prediction shows no recommendation and no confidence ("no prediction, no show"; unpredicted is never 50%). A Cyclotron prediction is a model's guess and never counts as a human rating or qualifies for a public page. A machine-proposed rating is at most 4; a 5 only comes from a person.

**Open questions.**
1. Training signal mapping: how do existing human signals become at-least-three versus below-three labels? Proposed: stars 3-5 = positive, 1-2 = negative; an accept with no stars is positive only if the site's default of 3 applies (decide), a reject without stars = negative; an accept recorded before stars existed; unrated rows stay unlabelled and teach nothing. Today stars are deliberately not sent to the Cyclotron (PPY-3247f1: "stars do not change the vote"); this story changes that and needs a decision on keeping accept/reject votes as a second signal.
2. Does the decision output stay a probability of accept, relabelled, or become a probability of >= 3 stars? What do existing models, the "recommended" status and thresholds mean after the change; is a retrain from star-labelled history needed, and is there enough history (88 of 149 MoM published Stories were unrated)?
3. Does a model also propose a number (3 or 4) as a "proposed rating" for review, or only the at-least-three decision? If it proposes, capped at 4, and shown as a proposal, never stored as starRating.
4. Per-section classifiers (PPY-0a285b): one at-least-three classifier per Section, or one per site?
5. Evaluation under the benchmark-parity protocol: measure against held-out star labels.

**Specification (outline).**
```gherkin
Feature: The rating classifier decides three stars or better
  Scenario: The decision is at-least-three versus below-three
    Given a Story or Reference the Cyclotron predicts on
    Then the question answered is "at least three stars or below three"
    And the prediction is stored as a prediction, never as the item's starRating

  Scenario: Human star ratings are the labels
    Given items rated by people with 4, 3 and 2 stars
    When the classifier is trained
    Then the 4 and 3 are positive examples and the 2 is a negative example
    And unrated items teach nothing

  Scenario: No prediction, no recommendation
    Given an item the classifier has not predicted on
    Then no recommendation, confidence or percentage is shown

  Scenario Outline: A machine-proposed rating is capped at four
    Given the classifier proposes a rating of <proposed>
    Then the stored proposal is <shown>
    Examples:
      | proposed | shown |
      | 3        | 3     |
      | 4        | 4     |
      | 5        | 4     |

  Scenario: A prediction never qualifies an item for a public page
    Given an unrated item predicted at-least-three with high confidence
    Then it is not listed on a public page (PPY-0e8d66)

  Scenario: Default rating is three
    Given a person accepts an item with no stars on a site using the default
    Then the open question 1 decides whether that counts as a 3; this scenario is completed when it is answered
```
